title: Habakkuk Bible Quiz - Chapter 3
description: Ten questions on Habakkuk 3: the prayer of Habakkuk, God coming from Teman, and joy in the God of salvation.

questions.text: How is this chapter introduced in the first verse?
questions.explanation: Habakkuk 3:1 introduces it as a prayer of Habakkuk, the prophet, set to victorious music.

answers.text: As a song of the watchmen on the walls
As a prayer of Habakkuk, set to victorious music
As a lament over the ruin of Nineveh
As a proverb spoken against the nations

questions.text: What does the prophet say Yahweh remembers in wrath?
questions.explanation: Habakkuk 3:2 says that in wrath, Yahweh remembers mercy.

questions.text: From where does verse 3 say God came?
questions.explanation: Habakkuk 3:3 says God came from Teman, the Holy One from Mount Paran.

questions.text: What is his splendor compared to?
questions.explanation: Habakkuk 3:4 says his splendor is like the sunrise, with rays shining from his hand.

questions.text: What went before him, according to verse 5?
questions.explanation: Habakkuk 3:5 says plague went before him, and pestilence followed his feet.

questions.text: Whose tents did the prophet see in affliction?
questions.explanation: Habakkuk 3:7 says he saw the tents of Cushan in affliction.

questions.text: What stood still in the sky?
questions.explanation: Habakkuk 3:11 says the sun and moon stood still in the sky at the light of his arrows.

questions.text: What happened to the prophet when he heard?
questions.explanation: Habakkuk 3:16 says he heard, and his body trembled, and his lips quivered at the voice.

questions.text: What does he say he will do even if the fig tree doesn't flourish and the fields yield no food?
questions.explanation: Habakkuk 3:17-18 says that though the fig tree doesn't flourish and the fields yield no food, yet he will rejoice in Yahweh.

questions.text: What does Yahweh make his feet like, according to the last verse?
questions.explanation: Habakkuk 3:19 says Yahweh is his strength, who makes his feet like deer's feet and enables him to go in high places.
